summary:
Space Mission Director is a browser game where players take the role of a mission director and plan a space mission from start to finish. It was built by the Cosmic Coders (Nisa, Javeria, Faisal and Mir) for the NASA Space Apps Challenge in Peshawar.

How it plays: You choose a mission (Earth Observation, Lunar or Mars), then build your spacecraft by adding instruments, a power source, an antenna, propulsion and a heat shield. Every part adds mass, cost and power use, so you have to balance them. Next you pick a rocket (small, medium or heavy) that can carry your craft without blowing the budget. The game checks your design for errors before you can launch.

What makes it interesting: Once you launch, random events like solar flares, fuel leaks, lost communication and meteor showers force you to make quick decisions, and your choices change the result. Each component comes with real facts and examples from missions like Voyager, Perseverance and Hubble, so players learn how real spacecraft work. Players can also explore the solar system and 170+ real spacecraft in 3D through NASA Eyes.

Why it matters: Instead of reading about engineering trade-offs, players experience them. The story intro with a choice of astronaut, a mission log and achievements keep it fun, and it runs in the browser with nothing to install.
details:
MISSION DIRECTOR – Beyond Earth

MISSION DIRECTOR – Beyond Earth is an interactive, browser-based educational space mission simulation game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Challenge #13: Space Mission Design Game.

The project allows players to experience the role of a space mission director by designing spacecraft, selecting scientific instruments, managing resources, choosing launch vehicles, and making critical decisions throughout a mission.

Players can choose between three mission types: Earth Observation, Lunar Exploration, and Mars Exploration. They must carefully balance spacecraft mass, power consumption, science capability, and budget while selecting suitable launch vehicles. The game provides live feedback on design choices and checks whether the spacecraft meets the mission requirements before launch.

An important feature is the dynamic mission event system, which introduces unexpected situations such as solar flares, fuel leaks, communication failures, meteor showers, and power surges. Players must make decisions to manage these challenges, making each mission more engaging and interactive.

The project also incorporates real-world space knowledge, including spacecraft facts and NASA Eyes, which provides access to more than 170 real spacecraft in 3D. It includes nine spacecraft components, three mission profiles, and six mission events.

Innovation and Impact:

Unlike traditional learning methods that mainly explain space engineering concepts theoretically, our game turns learning into an interactive experience. It helps students and beginners understand the challenges of real space mission planning through experimentation, problem-solving, resource management, and decision-making.

Our goal is to make space science and engineering more accessible, engaging, and enjoyable, especially for young learners and people interested in space exploration.

Tools and Development:

The project is developed as a browser-based interactive game, combining simulation mechanics, user interaction, educational content, and visual design. NASA-related spacecraft information and 3D visualization are incorporated to connect gameplay with real-world space exploration.

Team: Cosmic Coders
